data.abilityDescription: During basic training, Borr focused on hand-to-hand combat, and can carry out a variety of different moves in combat designed to knock around and reposition enemies, as well as prepare for enemy attacks.
data.level1Description: As a major action, you can push an enemy away from you, moving them from melee range of you to one turn away.
data.level2Description: As a major action, you can strike an enemy in the leg, preventing them from moving, charging or falling back as an action for their next turn. However they can still attack, dodge or do any other action that does not require a change in location.
data.level3Description: As a major action, you can now move with a target that you are grappling.
data.level4Description: As a major action, you brace for an attack, giving you 2 Natural Armour until the start of your next turn.
data.level5Description: For an extra 2 Focus, you can use any of the previous levels of this ability as a minor action.

data.abilityDescription: You use rats as scouts, taking advantage of their ability to move around unseen and unnoticed to gain information on enemy locations and building layouts, as well as possibly retrieving items and debilitating foes.
data.level1Description: Release a rat and give it an order. The rat can be ordered to scout ahead or to look around, and will report back, although it will not actually speak. You can only have one Rat Scout active at a time. The Rat Scout has +2 DEX and 2 Health.
data.level2Description: Your Rat Scout can now do basic physical tasks, such as pulling levers or picking up small objects.
data.level3Description: You are strongly bonded to your Rat Scout, allowing you to see what it sees and telepathically communicate with it whilst it is active.
data.level4Description: You can now get your rat to bite someone, causing them to throw up after a minute unless they pass a 15+ Endurance (Toxicity) check. The bite does not cause pain and is not noticeable. After an individual has been bitten, they cannot be bitten again for six hours.
data.level5Description: You can now have multiple Rat Scouts active at once, as a cost of 4 Focus per Rat Scout.

data.abilityDescription: You use a temporal device to accelerate time, allowing you to act far quicker than you otherwise would. Whilst initially this is compensated for by slowing you down, as you grow more competent you can accelerate time with no side effects.
data.level1Description: Speed up time, giving yourself an extra major and minor action. However, you lose your next turn. This ability can only be used once a round on your turn and doesn’t use up an action.
data.level2Description: You can now use Speed up Time on an ally, giving them an extra major and minor action but causing them to lose their next turn. You can do this once a round on their turn, and it uses up your next minor action.
data.level3Description: When you give yourself or an ally an extra major and minor action, you can now pick a different ally (or yourself) to lose their next turn.
data.level4Description: Take a minor action from an enemy. If you still have your minor action, then it combines with the enemy’s, removing both minor actions and giving you a major action. This can only be used once a round on your turn and doesn’t cost an action.
data.level5Description: Give yourself or an ally an extra major and minor action. This can only be done once a round on the turn of the character getting the actions and doesn’t cost an action.

data.abilityDescription: You disdain murder, and instead make every effort to non-lethally incapacitate foes, knocking them out and inflicting only non-permanent injuries.
data.level1Description: You no longer need to pass a Strength (Control) check when attempting to knock an enemy out instead of killing them, instead automatically knocking them out instead of killing them.

data.level1Description: If on your first turn of combat, you perform a melee, unarmed attack, it deals your maximum unarmed attack damage (if it hits).
data.level2Description: If on your first turn of combat, you perform a melee, unarmed attack, it cannot miss.
data.level3Description: If on your first turn of combat, you perform a melee, unarmed attack, it ignores all armour.
data.level4Description: If on your first turn of combat, you perform a melee, unarmed attack, it is an automatic critical hit.
data.level5Description: This ability now works for the first melee, unarmed attack you perform in a battle, whether or not it happens on your first turn of combat.

data.abilityDescription: When he fought in the arena, Ironhide was known for using rope to pull items towards him and hinder his enemy’s movements. Although he is no longer the fighter he once was, he has retained his skills with a rope.
data.level1Description: You have a lasso which you can use to pull small items up to a turn away into your hand. This level can be done as a minor action.
data.level2Description: You can now throw a lasso made of stronger rope. This lasso can be used to climb with, or pull an enemy from ranged to melee.
data.level3Description: You can now throw a net which can stop someone from moving, charging, falling back or fleeing for a round. You can also pull anything netted towards you for an additional 2 Focus.
data.level4Description: Your net is now a spiked net, dealing 2 damage a round to anyone or anything netted. The spiked net can also be laid out as a trap to catch enemies.
data.level5Description: Rather than an enemy automatically escaping the net after a round, they must now pass a 12+ Strength (Might) check to escape your net. Escaping the net is a major action.

data.abilityDescription: Your body automatically heals itself, wounds sealing themselves shut and restoring you, although it often is not powerful to fully restore you.
data.level1Description: If you took at least 2 damage last round, then at the start of your turn, you restore 2 Health. This ability doesn’t work when at zero Health or below.
data.level2Description: If you took at least 2 damage last round or if you are below 6 Health, restore 2 Health at the start of your turn. This ability doesn’t work when at zero Health or below. When out of combat, you are restored to 7 Health.
data.level3Description: When you take damage in a battle, you can spend 7 Focus to heal for 2+D4 Health. This can only be used immediately after the damage has been inflicted and cannot be used to heal more damage than was dealt to you. Using this ability uses up your next minor action.
data.level4Description: If you took at least 2 damage last round or if you are below 1/3 of your Max Health, restore 2 Health at the start of your turn. This ability doesn’t work when at zero Health or below. When out of combat, you are restored to 1/3 of your Max Health.
data.level5Description: Your regeneration now works when you are at zero Health and below.

data.abilityDescription: A glimmering shield surrounds you, a combination of Shadow Realm magic and Human Realm shield tech that prevents any damage from anyone who the shield does not recognise as having a similar personality.
data.level1Description:
You have a shield that negates all damage caused by anyone with a different personality to you. A personality does not have to be an exact match to damage through the shield, but they must be broadly similar e.g. both happy and excitable, or both easily angered and vengeful.
When you are first damaged in combat, the Psychometric Shield deactivates for five hours.

data.abilityDescription: You have been given a Personal Defence Drone, a basic drone used by individuals to protect them. It does this through a combination of scanning tools and forcefield projection, although more advanced models do have weaponry, to be used only in retaliation.
data.level1Description: You have an automated Personal Defence Drone that follows you. The Drone has no stats modifiers, has 4 Health and dodges any Strength (Attacking) checks made against it (although it can still be damaged if the damage dealt does not require a roll to hit). If destroyed, the drone requires one hour of repairs before it can be used again. Whilst the drone is active, Dexterity (Stealth) checks made against you or a group you are in has -5 as it scans the area.
data.level2Description: The drone projects a constant forcefield around you, giving you an additional +1 DEF (this stacks on top of any armour you already have).
data.level3Description: If you are about to take damage that would down or kill you, the drone intensifies the forcefield around you, reducing the damage you take by 4. This can only occur once per battle.
data.level4Description: Your drone now has access to a criminal database and facial recognition software and will alert you to the identity and crimes of any criminal it sees (assuming their crimes are logged in the database it draws from).
data.level5Description: Whenever you take damage, the enemy that damaged you takes D5 damage as the drone automatically shoots them with a plasma blast.

data.abilityDescription: Sarsha has trained herself in the use of firearms, using her mathematical expertise to fire shots that ricochet from surface to surface, before striking an enemy in their weakest point.
data.level1Description: You make Intelligence (Anatomy) checks to attack, instead of Strength (Attacking).
data.level2Description: You have a +2 to hit when attacking with a Sniper, provided you have not moved your turn before. This ability does not stack.
data.level3Description: Any Snipers you attack with always deal at least 2 damage when they hit (for example, a D8 weapon becomes 2+D6).
data.level4Description: You critically hit on a 19 as well as a 20.
data.level5Description: If one of your attacks with a Sniper reduces an enemy to 2 or less Health, then their Health is automatically reduced to zero.

data.abilityDescription: Whether its two swords locked together, or two beams of energy pushing against each other, you and your enemy clash for dominance, with the winner pushing through their foes attack.
data.level1Description: If an enemy is about to deal damage to you and you have a  weapon of the same damage type, then you clash with them. Both you and the enemy roll weapon damage. Whoever’s is higher deals the difference in damage to their opponent. If your opponent wins, then that attack only cost them a minor action instead of a major. Using this ability uses up your next minor action unless you win, in which case it uses no action.

data.abilityDescription: You have no honour and will do anything to win. This includes underhanded attacks, striking when enemies are distracted, and even feigning surrender to get enemies to let down their guard.
data.level1Description: When combat starts, you can quickly throw an underhanded attack, dealing D4 damage to an enemy of your choice within one turn.
data.level2Description: If an enemy did not target you with any actions during their last turn, and instead targeted one of your allies, then on your turn, you can spend 4 Focus when you attack to give yourself a +4 to hit and, if you hit, you deal extra damage equal to half your damage roll. This cannot be used at the same time as a Stealth attack.
data.level3Description: You sucker punch an enemy in melee range, dealing D4 damage and causing them to lose D6 Focus. This can be done as a minor action. This cannot be used more than once on the same enemy during the same combat encounter.
data.level4Description: Launch two attacks against an enemy. The enemy has +3 to dodge against your first attack. However, if the first attack hits, the second attack deals double damage if it hits. If the first attack misses, the second attack is a normal attack.
data.level5Description: Make a Charisma (Performance) check against an enemy’s Willpower (Pressure). If your Current Health is lower than the enemy’s Current Health then you get a +6 to this check. If you succeed, then you get to launch an attack, automatically hitting the target and dealing double damage. You get a -10 debuff to this check if you attempt to use it on an enemy you have used it on in the past. This debuff stacks.

data.level1Description: You have a Gryphon that accompanies you. Your Gryphon has 7 Health, 3 Focus and +1 Strength. If your Gryphon loses all of its Health, it must recover for 8 hours before it can be used again.
data.level2Description: Your Gryphon can now be mounted, and used to fly, although it can only carry one person on its back, and another in its claws.
data.level3Description: Your Gryphon now has a 1+D4 Slashing Talon attack (Melee only), +1 Dexterity and an extra 3 Focus.
data.level4Description:
You have a magical whistle that you can you to call your Gryphon. The Gryphon can hear the whistle no matter where it is, and will come to you when you use it. 
The Gryphon also gains Unnatural Strength ability (4 Focus):
Draw upon your reserves of strength, allowing you to carry incredibly heavy loads (with an upper limit of around a car full of people) for one minute.
data.level5Description:
Your Gryphon now has 13 Health, an extra 3 Focus (9 in total), an extra +2 Strength, +1 Dexterity and +1 Intelligence.

Abigail also gains the Magical Sight ability (3 Focus): See magical energy for ten minutes.

data.abilityDescription: Through a combination of cutting edge genetic engineering and mutagenic chemicals, you take on the properties of dragons, becoming more and more draconic until eventually you can transform into a full dragon, although the amount of time you can do this for is limited to avoid your body burning out.
data.level1Description: You are covered in scales, giving you 1 Natural Armour, and have long claws. Your unarmed attack deals D8 Slashing damage (Melee only).
data.level2Description: You have a long, spiked tail that you can attack with for 1+D4 Crushing damage (Melee only). When you hit an enemy with your tail, they must make a 12+ Endurance (Impact) check or be knocked a turn away from you.
data.level3Description: Armoured, reptilian wings sprout from your shoulders. Whilst you cannot use these to fly yet, when you are falling from a great height, spend 5 Focus to flap your wings, allowing you to land safely without taking any damage.
data.level4Description:
Unleash a breath of fire at an enemy within one turn of you. The fire breath deals 4+D6 damage to that enemy and half damage to all enemies within melee range of your target.
After using your fire breath, you cannot use it again for five rounds.

You also have a bite attack which deals 2D6 Puncturing damage (Melee only).
data.level5Description: Transform into a dragon for fifteen minutes. When in dragon form, you can fly and are considered mounted at all times. You cannot speak and have +5 Strength and Endurance (giving you +10 Health), but a -4 to all Dexterity (Dodging) checks. You have 2 Natural Armour when in dragon form. You can only attack with your Claws, Tail, Fire Breath and Bite, but these all deal an extra D10 damage. You can cancel your dragon form at any time. When in dragon form, you can eat a dead body to lower the amount of time until you can use your fire breath again by 1 round. This can be done as a minor action or can be done if you kill an enemy with a bite attack for no action. Enemies have a -12 to checks made to grapple you unless they match or exceed you in size.

data.abilityDescription: Your form is incredibly malleable, allowing you to turn your body into a liquid-like state whilst retaining your sentience.
data.level1Description: You can change your arms into any shape you want, although they must retain roughly the same volume. You can use this to change your arms into melee weapons. Attacking with these weapons deals 3+DX damage, where X is your level.
data.level2Description: You can now pool excess mass in your body, allowing you to change your arms into small objects like keys and tools, as long as they are stationary objects. You can use this to gain a +4 to Dexterity (Lockpicking) checks by changing your finger into a key.
data.level3Description: Turn your whole body into liquid for five seconds, or one round if in combat. When in liquid form you can move as a minor action, allowing you to slip through small cracks. You still take damage normally when in liquid form.
data.level4Description: When in liquid form, you can extend the amount of time you are a liquid by 3 Focus for every 5 seconds, or one combat round. This does not take an action to do.
data.level5Description: You now have +3 to dodge and take 3 less damage from all attacks when in liquid form.

data.abilityDescription: Manid is a Pholi, a small, pangolin-like race that have not yet mastered spaceflight. Manid owes Eltha a life debt after she saved him from an artillery strike and helps where he can, although he will not put himself in life-threatening situations.
data.level1Description: You are accompanied by Manid, a small, brown-scaled attendant. Manid has 10 Health, +2 CHA, +2 END and -1 WIL (His endurance modifier is already added to his Health.) Manid can do a number of things, such as buying items (if given money), delivering messages and talking to people. However, he will not do anything that will risk his own life, including combat. If Manid loses all of his Health, he is not killed but must recover for 6 hours before doing anything.
data.level2Description: N/A
data.level3Description: N/A
data.level4Description: N/A
data.level5Description: N/A

data.abilityDescription: A waste product of the Hellhound Exoskeleton’s perpetual furnace is a collection of noxious gases. However even these have been turned into a weapon, with the gases stored in tanks, ready to be unleashed against the wearer’s enemies.
data.level1Description: Spray an enemy within one turn of you with a blast of poisonous gas, reducing either their Intelligence, Willpower, Perception or Charisma by 3 for three rounds, or five minutes if out of combat. Which stat is reduced is up to the players. This can be done without alerting the target if the player passes a 12+ Dexterity (Stealth) check.
data.level2Description: You can now use your Noxious Fumes to reduce an enemy’s Strength, Endurance or Dexterity. This reduction works in the same way as Level 1.
data.level3Description: Instead of reducing a stat of your choice, you can now use your Noxious Fumes to reduce an enemies Focus by 4+D6. This reduction lasts for three rounds or five minutes if out of combat, and can be done without alerting the target if the player passes a 12+ Dexterity (Stealth) check.
data.level4Description: You can now use your Noxious Fumes to reduce the damage an enemy deals by two for three rounds. This damage reduction is taken into account before armour and cannot be done without alerting the target.
data.level5Description: When you use Noxious Fumes, you can now choose two effects from the previous levels to afflict a target with.

data.abilityDescription: Your form is made up of a collection of smaller individuals, be they a swarm of animals, a spreading mass of fungus, or a collection of tiny robots. This allows you to grow and diminish in size based on the number of individuals making you up.
data.level1Description: You have different forms, dependant on your current Health. When you have at least 1/3 of your Max Health, you are in a humanoid form and deal 2D4 Piercing damage (Melee only). When below 1/3 of your Max Health, you are in a diminished form, which deals 1D4 damage, has -2 to all stats except END, and +4 DEX. Changing forms happens automatically and doesn’t take an action. At any time you can lower your health to drop down a form as a minor action.
data.level2Description: When in your diminished form, you can climb on walls without needing to roll, and can spend 5 Focus to automatically flee a battle without being attacked or chased.
data.level3Description: When you have at least 2/3 of your max Health, you can now transform into a giant form. Your giant form is eight foot, deals 3D4 damage, has +2 END (although this does not give you any extra Health), +4 STR and -5 DEX. You also gain the ability Take Blow, which allows you to take an attack intended for another player for 4 Focus, with the attack dealing 2 less damage. If your Health drops below 2/3 of your Max Health, you are forced back into your humanoid form.
data.level4Description: When in diminished form, you can now split your body up to pass through any space larger than one of the individuals you are made up of. When in your giant form, you now have a 6 Focus Bludgeon ability that deals 4+D12 damage to an enemy. The enemy must also make a 12+ Endurance (Impact) check, losing a minor action if they pass and a major if they fail.
data.level5Description: Turn yourself into a tide of your constituent individuals that covers the whole battlefield for one round. You have no set location and can divide up 6D4 of damage across any targets on the battlefield. Attacks against you can’t miss, but any enemies in the tide must pass a 13+ Willpower (Courage) check to attack, and a 15+ Endurance (Fatigue) check to move. This ability can be extended for further rounds at a cost of 4 Focus per round. You cannot use this in diminished form.

data.abilityDescription: As you duck and weave between enemy attacks, you fire off small attacks of your own. Whilst not the most damaging, these quick attacks still hurt, and can quickly build up.
data.level1Description: When you dodge an enemy attack with a dodge roll that is at least 7 higher than the enemy’s attack roll, deal 2 damage to that enemy.

data.level1Description: You have a messenger bird which can carry written messages to people, assuming you know the rough location of that person. The bird is also to find and return to you even if you move from the location you were in when you sent it off.

data.abilityDescription:
You aim for a specific part of an enemy’s body, crippling that body part if you hit, although your focus on your target does make the blow easier to avoid.
(This ability has additional supporting information)
data.level1Description: When you attack an enemy, you aim for a specific body part. This attack has a -3 to hit, but weakens the enemy if you hit, based on where you targeted. A target can have multiple different body parts hit in the same combat, although hitting the same kind of body part more than once has no additional effect. This ability only costs 3 Focus if it misses.

data.abilityDescription: You travel with an apprentice; someone who seeks to learn from you. As you journey together, your apprentice will grow in skill, following your example until they are ready to make their own way in the world.
data.level1Description: You are accompanied by an apprentice who seeks to learn from you. The apprentice has 8 Health (before Endurance modifiers), 15 Focus, two weapon skills and 3 stat points that roughly mirror your stat spread, as well as a D4 weapon in an appropriate weapon type. Your apprentice can assist you in a number of ways. If your apprentice loses all of their Health, they must recover for 12 hours before they can do anything.
data.level2Description: Your apprentice gains 2 stat points and a specialty. What these stats and specialties are depends on what they have been doing since joining you.
data.level3Description: Your apprentice’s weapon is now a D6. When your apprentice loses all of their Health, they can now recover after 6 hours.
data.level4Description: Your apprentice gains 2 Health and 2 specialties of their choice. They can also choose between their weapon upgrading to a D8 or gaining 1 armour in a type of their choice.
data.level5Description: Your apprentice gains 2 Overcharges and a number of abilities equal to you (these abilities start at Level 1), becoming a fully-fledged Level 1 character that can level up and be played as any other character. However, your apprentice can now be permanently killed in the same way as any other character.

data.abilityDescription: As an investigator, Lawrence needs to be able to follow up on leads and discern clues regarding the various strange phenomena throughout the City. Deciding to specialise in problems of a magical nature, he has picked up various skills, technologies and magics of his own that he can use to investigate magical occurrences.
data.level1Description: You detect anything around you that is magical in nature. This does not tell you what the magic does or anything else about it.
data.level2Description: You are aware of when a powerful piece of magic is being used within a few hours walking distance of you, and the approximate location of the magic.
data.level3Description: When in close proximity to a piece of magic or an area where magic has been used within a week, you can discern the purpose of that magic.
data.level4Description: When discerning the purpose of a piece of magic, you can spend 3 extra Focus to determine who or what cast that magic.
data.level5Description: When in an area where magic has been cast within the last year, you can have a vision of the moment the magic was cast, seeing it as if you were there.

data.abilityDescription: As an enemy strikes you, you turn on them with a terrifying stare, making them rethink their life choices and tremble in fear, affecting their combat ability.
data.level1Description: The first enemy who deals damage to you in combat suffers a -3 to Strength (Attacking) checks unless they pass a 17+ Willpower (Courage) check.

data.abilityDescription: As a Griot of the Sea Scorpion Clan, you can transform into a Sea Scorpion hybrid form. Your grow chitinous plates and a powerful tails made for swimming. You secrete a slowing poison and are naturally intimidating, drawing enemy attacks towards you.
data.level1Description: Transform into a Sea Scorpion/Human Hybrid for two hours. When in your Hybrid form, you have +1 STR, +2 DEX and +2 Natural armour. Your damaging attacks now inflict a poison that reduces an enemy’s DEX by 2 until the end of combat. This poison can stack up to a -6. When in Hybrid form, you instantly pass all Endurance (Swimming) checks, and enemies have a 50% chance to attack you in combat over other targets.

data.abilityDescription: You are an expert at making the most out of your vehicle’s weapons, able to quickly repair them, increase their firepower and target specific enemy systems.
data.level1Description: Repair a damaged or destroyed weapon system for a vehicle without needing to make an Intelligence (Engineering) check. This still uses up your vehicle's minor action.
data.level2Description: Overload or amp up a vehicle weapon’s capabilities. This causes it to deal 50% more damage for a single attack, but deals D6 damage to you. This does not take an action to do.
data.level3Description: When a vehicle weapon is used to attack an enemy vehicle, you can target a specific system, assuming you know that system exists. This attack has -3 to hit. This does not take an action to do.
data.level4Description: Lower the time it takes to repair a damaged or destroyed vehicle weapon system by one round. This does not take an action to do, and can be used multiple times at once to lower the time by more than one round.
data.level5Description: Level 2 of this ability is now a permanent, passive effect, and you are no longer damaged when you increase the damage of a vehicle weapon attack.

data.abilityDescription: As a gremlin, Vex is blessed with the ability to go unnoticed if he wants. Combined with his small size, this can make him incredibly hard to spot, with people’s eyes simply passing over him without even acknowledging his presence.
data.level1Description: You do not trigger technology or magic-based motion detectors.
data.level2Description: When you flee a battle, you won’t be attacked or chased unless there are no other targets.
data.level3Description: If you are in stealth and you are about to be caught, you instead aren’t.
data.level4Description: If an ally nearby is about to fail a stealth check, you can increase the result of the check by 2. This ability can be used multiple times as part of the same action.
data.level5Description: Enemies don’t notice you, allowing you to start a battle in Stealth.

data.abilityDescription:
You manipulate luck to cause you and your allies’ attacks to strike true, coincidentally hitting enemies in their weakest points.

Requires Manipulator of Luck ability
data.level1Description: Increase the result of a damage roll by 1. This does not take an action to do and can be used multiple times as part of a single damage roll.

data.abilityDescription: The Raven Captains fight alongside Inanimates, victims of the Hraf Z-12 Formula that have been converted into faceless black figures that obey any commands without hesitation.
data.level1Description: Summon Inanimate soldiers at a cost of 5 Focus per soldier. Each Inanimate soldier has 3 Health, +3 to hit, -4 to dodge and a D4 Wounding Rifle. If the soldier is killed, any remaining damage can be directed at a different target. The ability can be combined with other levels of this ability to summon different Inanimates as a single major action. The Inanimate soldiers last for 24 hours.
data.level2Description: Summon Inanimate meat shields at a cost of 4 Focus per meat shield. Each meat shield has 5 Health, +1 to hit, -4 to dodge and a D4-1 Piercing Small Melee weapon. If the meat shield is killed, any remaining damage can be directed at a different target. The ability can be combined with other levels of this ability to summon different Inanimates as a single major action. The Inanimate meat shields last for 24 hours.
data.level3Description: Your Inanimate soldiers now attack for D6 damage.
data.level4Description: Your Inanimate meat shields must now be killed before any of its allies can be attacked.
data.level5Description: Summon Inanimate heavy troopers at a cost of 10 Focus per heavy trooper. Each Inanimate heavy trooper has 5 Health, and a D4 Blasting Electro-Cannon that deals double damage to vehicles or inorganic foes and damages all targets in melee range of its target if it hits. If the heavy trooper is killed, any remaining damage can be directed at a different target. The ability can be combined with other levels of this ability to summon different Inanimates as a single major action. The Inanimate heavy troopers last for 24 hours.

data.abilityDescription: Fighting from the back, you chip away at enemies with long-range attacks, protecting your allies and quickly changing position before any enemies can close in on you.
data.level1Description: If you are wielding a ranged weapon, and you did not use your major action during your turn, then you can attack an enemy on their turn immediately after they attack an ally within attackable range. You gain a +3 to hit with this attack. This ability does not take an action to do. The other levels of this ability can also only be used when wielding ranged weapons.
data.level2Description: If an enemy attacks you and your Dexterity (Dodging) check exceeds their Strength (Attacking) check by at least 8, you can spend 5 Focus to immediately launch an attack against them, assuming they are within attackable range. You have a +3 to hit with this attack. This ability does not take an action to do.
data.level3Description: When an enemy attacks you in melee, after the damage has been dealt, you can spend 4 Focus to immediately move one turn away from it. This ability uses up your next minor action. You can use Level 2 of this ability after using this to move one turn away from the enemy.
data.level4Description: If an enemy moves out of melee range of one of your allies, you can spend 5 Focus to launch an attack against them. You have a +3 to hit with this attack. This does not take an action to do.
data.level5Description: Every time you launch an attack against an enemy when it isn’t your turn, an ally of your choice restores 3 Focus.

data.abilityDescription: Derp is a minor demon that is said to be as old as the Shadow Realm itself. Whilst it appears no different from an ordinary pug, save for it’s red eyes and horns, it is completely indestructible, with the most powerful of Gods and demon kings being completely unable to even scratch it.
data.level1Description: You have a small demonic pug named Derp. Derp is very loyal and loveable, has +3 to Charisma and a -2 to all other stats. Derp is indestructible and cannot be damaged or killed. Derp is not very smart or capable, but is willing to try anything you ask it to do. If separated from you for more than 4 hours, Derp teleports to your position.

data.abilityDescription: Cybernetically enhanced as a child, you are now more machine than man. These robotic components have given you a great deal of extra tools at your disposal, although you require regular charging.
data.level1Description:
You can charge yourself at electrical ports and sockets around The City, giving you one Electrical Charge (EC) per hour you spend charging. You can hold a maximum of 3 EC.

You can spend 1 EC to generate small amounts of electricity which you can use to charge small devices, create sparks, and for a variety of other, non-combat uses.
data.level2Description: Fire a bolt of electricity at an enemy within one turn of you, dealing 4+D4 damage.
data.level3Description: Unleash a blast of electrical energy, disabling all electrical devices, including electrical weapons around you for a minute, or until three individuals, not including you, have taken their turn.
data.level4Description: You can now hold 5 Electrical Charges (EC), and each charge now only takes 30 minutes to charge.
data.level5Description: Clap your hands together, unleashing a massive electrical burst. The burst deals 4+D4 damage to all enemies within one turn of you and stuns them for X rounds, making them unable to attack or move and causing them to suffer a -4 to any dodge rolls.

data.abilityDescription: Mirid has learnt the art of tracking, using it to not only track animals, but to determine the location of people, and even leave scent marks on them that he can follow up on.
data.level1Description: You can use Perception (Tracking) to tell if you are being followed or tracked.
data.level2Description: When examining footprints, you can automatically tell what species the footprints belong to, even if you fail a Perception (Tracking) check to follow them.
data.level3Description: You know the last person to have touched/been in proximity to any inanimate object.
data.level4Description: Instantly pass a Perception (Tracking) check. This can be done after rolling.
data.level5Description: Secretly mark a target with a touch. You can then track that person’s movements from where you marked them for 24 hours, or until they wash the scent mark off/change clothes if their clothes were touched. Multiple targets can be marked at once.

data.abilityDescription: As your enemy strikes you, you pivot, hitting them with the force of their own attack and causing you both to become injured.
data.level1Description: When you take melee damage, instead only take half. Your attacker takes the other half. Both halves ignore any armour or damage reduction effects.

data.level1Description: Enhance an already present emotion in a target you are looking at. This can be used for a variety of reasons, such as making a target happier and more amenable to you, or enhancing anger to incite violence.

data.abilityDescription: You can now blast enemies with fire, burning them to a crisp and drawing on flames in the world to increase your effectiveness. However, this increases your own Heat, potentially leading to a fiery explosion if not properly managed.
data.level1Description:
You now have a Heat gauge. If you reach 15 Heat you explode, reducing your Heat to zero and dealing 40 fire damage to yourself and everyone within two turns of you.
You have a 4+D4 Fireball attack (Melee and Ranged). Attacking with this generates 1 Heat.
You can spend X Focus to lower your Heat by X.
data.level2Description: You heat your skin to great temperatures, causing any enemy that successfully attacks you in melee to take 4 damage, ignoring armour. This can be activated or deactivated as a minor action and generates 3 Heat every round.
data.level3Description: You will now not explode until you reach 20 Heat, and you can now lower your Heat as a minor action.
data.level4Description: You can now absorb the energy from fires out in the world. When you do this, your Heat increases from 1-10, with the exact amount based on the size of the fire absorbed, but your next fire attack that hits will deal additional fire damage equal to the Heat you gained.
data.level5Description: Explode your Heat early, dealing double your current Heat in fire damage to yourself and everyone within two turns of you. This reduces your Heat to zero.

data.abilityDescription: You have the kind of face that puts people at ease, helping them to open up to you and allowing you to talk them into things they might otherwise have refused to do.
data.level1Description: Gain +5 to a Charisma (Charm) check. This can be done after rolling for the check.

data.abilityDescription: The Hounds of Thor, whilst not being beasts from actual myth, are wolf-like spirit beasts that have been imbued with electrical magic in hour of the Norse god. They are a dangerous threat and are adept at singling out and taking down specific targets.
data.level1Description: Summon two Hounds of Thor to aid you in combat. Each Hound has 8 Health, 8 Focus, +2 STR and +1 DEX, as well as a D6 Shocking Bite attack (Melee only). The hounds last until killed or the end of combat.
data.level2Description: When you summon your Hounds of Thor, pick out a specific target. The Hounds have +2 to hit and deal 1 extra damage against that target.
data.level3Description: Your Hounds now have 12 Health, +3 STR and +2 DEX.
data.level4Description:
Your Hounds gain the Bolt and Paralysing Shock ability.
Bolt (5 Focus)- Deal D8 damage to an enemy, ignoring armour.
Paralysing Shock (3 Focus)- Latch onto a target with your jaws and lightly shock them, causing them to lose their minor action. If the target has already lost their minor action this round, they lose their major action.
data.level5Description: Your Hounds can now run through the air on trails of lightning, allowing them to fly.

data.abilityDescription: As an ex-officer, Faribir is adept at getting the best out of the people he is with, inspiring and, in some cases, forcing them to achieve greater results.
data.level1Description: If an ally rolls minimum weapon damage when attacking an enemy, spend 2 Focus to add 1 to their damage. This does not cost an action and cannot be used to increase your own damage.
data.level2Description: When a nearby ally uses an ability, you can split the Focus cost evenly between you and the ally. If the ability has an odd cost, the ally pays more.
data.level3Description: If an ally draws on a check, you can spend 4 Focus to instead have them win the check. This does not cost an action if used in combat and cannot be used to pass a check you are making.
data.level4Description: When an ally critically fails, make a 12+ Willpower (Presence) check. If you succeed, the failure is treated as a normal failure instead of a critical failure. This does not cost an action if used in combat, does not change the check result, and cannot be used if you critically fail.
data.level5Description: Give all allies +3 to a stat of your choice for a short time, or the rest of the battle if in combat.

data.abilityDescription: Learning other languages has always come easily to you. As well as speaking multiple languages, you can pick up other languages easier than most.
data.level1Description: As well as your native language, you can speak one additional language of your choice. When coming across a language you don’t speak, you can spend 6 hours interacting with people speaking that language to gain a +2 bonus to language checks when trying to understand the language. This stacks until you have spent 60 hours learning the language, at which point you can speak and understand it.

data.abilityDescription: You wield the powers of the God Aran, powers that are especially harmful to those who have wronged others. Attacks are drawn towards these individuals, burning away at them with a smoky grey magic.
data.level1Description: Each person you meet now has a Vengeance Rating from 0 to 10, depending on how many people in the world would like revenge on them, with 10 being a figure against whom whole nations or massive groups of people would like revenge on. When sleeping, your Mindset is now equal to half the average Vengeance Rating of those you have killed that day. This cannot increase your Mindset above 5.
data.level2Description: Against targets with a Vengeance Rating of 6 or above, you can roll twice when rolling to hit, and take the higher result.
data.level3Description: Create a shield of swirling grey energy that defends against the attacks of a target of your choice. Any attacks made by that target against you damage the shield first. The Shield has Health equal to the target’s Vengeance Rating.
data.level4Description: Against targets with a Vengeance Rating of 6 or above, you deal extra damage equal to half their Vengeance Rating, rounding down.
data.level5Description: Unleash a blast of energy that harnesses the power of the unavenged. The blast does damage to a target equal to their Vengeance Rating times 3.

data.abilityDescription: Using high-tech goggles, you analyse the flow of electricity, allowing you to pick out wiring, electrical systems and defences, and even robots and drones.
data.level1Description: You can see the flow of electricity through wires and electrical systems for one minute. You cannot move whilst your Electrical Vision is active.
data.level2Description: You can now move whilst your Electrical Vision is active.
data.level3Description: When activating your Electrical Vision, you can spend an extra 2 Focus to see the flow of electricity even through a surface, although you cannot see them if they are behind multiple surfaces.
data.level4Description: Your Electrical Vision now lasts for ten minutes.
data.level5Description: Your Electrical Vision is now always active as a permanent passive effect. Level 3 of this ability is now activated independently to allow you to see the flow of electricity through a single surface for ten minutes.

data.abilityDescription: You are able to appraise machines and mechanical devices at a glance, evaluating their systems and discovering weaknesses in their systems that can be exploited.
data.level1Description: Instantly pass an Intelligence (Engineering) check when rolling to study or analyse a robot, cyborg or similar mechanical device. This can be done after rolling for the check. All attacks made against mechanical foes you have studied deal +2 damage.

You carry with you a bag of guns, containing everything from a toy pellet gun to a minigun. In battle, you draw a weapon randomly and open fire.

data.level1Description: You are skilled in all weapon types but have no starting weapon. When you begin combat, you draw a random weapon from your bag of firearms and use that weapon for the rest of the battle, with the weapon going back into the bag when combat ends.

data.abilityDescription: You are in possession of potent chemicals, whether these are pills or injections. These can have a variety of different effects, but they are always intense, and always come with a downside. As your skill, grows, you can deduce what some of these doses do, allowing you to slightly influence the effects.
data.level1Description: Gain +10 to a random specialty, and -10 to a different random specialty. This effect lasts until one of these specialties has been rolled. You can also replace these by taking another dose.
data.level2Description: You can now give power doses to another person, at a cost of 6 Focus per dose.
data.level3Description: Gain +10 to a random specialty in a stat of your choice, and -10 to a different random specialty. This effect lasts until one of these specialties has been rolled. You can also replace these by taking another dose.
data.level4Description: Gain +10 to a random specialty in a stat of your choice, and -10 to a different random specialty in a stat of your choice. This effect lasts until one of these specialties has been rolled. You can also replace these by taking another dose.
data.level5Description: You may now reroll your positive or negative specialty bonus within the same stat, at a cost of 3 focus per reroll. Each time you reroll, you cannot get any of the same specialties you previously received this use.

data.abilityDescription: You pull a pistol out of a hidden pocket and fire a quick shot at a nearby target.
data.level1Description: Fire a quick pistol shot, dealing 2 damage to an enemy. This can be used at any time and doesn’t cost an action to do.

data.abilityDescription: You spent some time on Elestratus, the mythical moving city of the God Fulgaram. During your time there, you interacted with the underwater races that make the city their home, and picked up knowledge and artifacts, as well as a natural resistance to electricity.
data.level1Description: You automatically pass all Intelligence (Cultures) or (Geography) checks when rolling for information related to Fulgaram or Elestratus.
data.level2Description: You can speak the language of any sentient underwater or amphibious race.
data.level3Description: You have an Amulet of Five-Twelve Breath which allows you to hold your breath for an hour.
data.level4Description: When you are damaged by electricity, you only take half damage, gaining the other half in Focus.
data.level5Description: When sleeping in a storm, you always have a Location rating of 5, and gain a +1 to your Mindset. This cannot increase your Mindset above a 5.

data.abilityDescription: You speed allows you to dodge enemy attacks with ease, launching attacks and moving around the battlefield as they leave themselves open.
data.level1Description: If you dodge an attack with a dodge roll at least 4 higher than the enemy’s attack roll, spend 1 Focus to gain a minor action. If you dodge an attack with a dodge roll at least 7 higher than the enemy’s attack roll, spend 3 Focus to gain a major action. Gaining actions in this way does not take an action to do.

data.abilityDescription: You are skilled at gaining information from people. You know how to talk to people, can easily ingratiate yourself with local populations, and can pick out those with important information, even predicting their actions.
data.level1Description: After talking with someone for at least one minute, spend 3 Focus to know which Charisma specialty will be most effective when trying to get them to do a specific thing, and which specialty will be least effective.
data.level2Description: If you wish to know a piece of information that is known by the majority of the population of your current location, you can learn it after spending 5 Focus and ten minutes walking amongst and interacting with the local population.
data.level3Description: Identify an individual in line of sight that could provide useful information or is in some way related to your objective, assuming that such an individual exists.
data.level4Description: If you have spent at least one day amongst a people whose language you do not speak, then you can spend 4 Focus when someone speaks to you using that language to pass an Intelligence (Languages) check, allowing you to understand the general gist of what that person is saying. This must be done before rolling for the check.
data.level5Description: After observing someone for an hour or talking with them for fifteen minutes, spend 6 Focus and make a 13+ Perception (Empathy) check. If you succeed, then you can accurately predict that individual’s next action. Once you attempt the check, your observation/talking time is reset and you must begin again.

data.abilityDescription: You have an affinity for rats, worms, spiders and other crawling, unloved creatures. Whilst you can’t literally talk with them, you can collect basic information, communicate simple ideas and even give them orders.
data.level1Description: You can commune with Rats, Worms and other verminous creatures. Whilst they will not be able to speak, they can convey simple messages and information.

data.level1Description: An enemy within one turn of you rolls a D12, taking however much they roll below a 10 in damage. This attack costs no Focus and is a minor action if it deals no damage.

data.abilityDescription:
You wield the weapon of a Magician; playing cards that use both technology and magic to provide a variety of different effects. These cards are devastating and make a Magician a terrifying and versatile foe.
(This ability has additional supporting information)
data.level1Description: Instead of a weapon, you have a deck of magical playing cards. When you start combat, you draw five cards. The cards have different effects depending on what card it is. Using any number of cards in your turn is a major action, except for the suit of Diamonds, which do not take an action. On your turn, you can draw back up to five cards as a major action.
data.level2Description: As a minor action, change the suit of one of the cards in your hand.
data.level3Description: Pull an extra Joker out of your sleeve and use it. This can be done as a minor action.
data.level4Description: Draw back up to five cards. This can be done as a minor action but can only be done once per round. You cannot use any of the cards you have drawn until your next turn.
data.level5Description: You now have two decks of cards, and each hand draws independently from a different deck, allowing you to wield ten cards in total.

data.abilityDescription: Using advanced technology, you generate matter out of basically nothing, creating shapes and weapons out of a variety of materials.
data.level1Description: You can create basic shapes out of plastic, metal or carbon fibre. You cannot create weapons or anything with moving parts, but can create simple shapes for a variety of uses, including ladder shapes or blocks to weigh things down etc. The Focus cost varies based on the size and complexity of what you are making.
data.level2Description: When you are done with an object, you can reabsorb it to gain half the Focus cost of creating it back.
data.level3Description: You can now use your Create Object to make a basic melee weapon of any melee weapon type. You cannot use this to create a weapon with any moving parts. The weapon deals 1+D6 damage.
data.level4Description: You can now use your Create Object to create a barricade that absorbs 5 damage before breaking. This can be done as a minor action.
data.level5Description: You can now create objects with simple moving parts, such as gears or cogs, and can now make basic ranged weapons as well as melee weapons (the ranged weapons also deal 1+D6 damage). You still cannot make anything electronic or electrical in nature.

data.abilityDescription: Whilst gunpowder may be a secret known only to pirates, you have the next best thing. Bundles of Fracture Spines that, when broken, unleash a blast of concussive air powerful enough to crack stone.
data.level1Description: Throw a Fracture Spine bundle at an enemy up to two turns away. The bundle explodes after D4-1 turns, dealing 5 damage to all targets within D3-1 turns of the original target (with 0 turns counting as everyone within melee of the target). This can also be used out of combat as an explosive device.
data.level2Description: Instead of rolling D4-1 to determine when the bundle explodes, you can now choose before you throw it, ranging from exploding on the turn you throw it, to up to 4 turns later.
data.level3Description: Before you throw the bundle you can coat it in a sticky substance, causing it to stick to the original target and move with them. You may also use this out of combat to make the bomb stick to whatever it is thrown at.
data.level4Description: Instead of rolling D3-1 to determine when the radius of the blast, you can now choose before you throw it, ranging from damaging only the original target, to everyone within 2 turns.
data.level5Description: Before throwing the bundle, you may now increase the damage it deals to all targets by X/2. Increasing the damage increases the intensity of the blast when used out of combat.

data.abilityDescription: You protect your weaker allies by positioning yourself as the greater threat, striking out against foes that strike your armour and and taking mortal blows meant for your allies.
data.level1Description: Taunt enemies within two turns, giving them a 50% chance to attack you over other targets within attackable range when they attack. This lasts until the end of combat or until cancelled. You can cancel this effect on your turn and cancelling this ability doesn’t take an action.
data.level2Description: When you are downed, you launch an attack against the enemy who downed you.
data.level3Description: If an ally is about to be downed, you can redirect the attack to yourself. You are brought down to the Health your ally would’ve been reduced to. This doesn’t take an action to do.
data.level4Description: If an attack made against you is completely absorbed by your armour, you can launch an attack against that target, dealing half damage if you hit.
data.level5Description: Whilst conscious, you cannot be moved against your will unless the thing trying to move you passes an 18+ Strength (Might) check.

data.abilityDescription: You can expel both shadow and light, infusing it into weapons or people, or simply firing it as a bolt. However, these energies are antithetical to each other, and you never know which of the two you will channel in any given moment.
data.level1Description: At the start of your turn, you can spend 1 Focus to roll a D4. If you roll a 1 or a 2, then your weapon deals an extra 3 damage. If you roll a 3 or a 4, then your weapon heals you for 3 Health every time you deal damage with it. Only one of these effects can be active on your weapon at a time, and the effect lasts until you use this ability to change it. This does not take an action to do.
data.level2Description: Imbue your Shadowlight into a light source you can see, rolling a D4. If you roll a 1 or 2, you extinguish the light source for 24 hours. If you roll a 3 or a 4, you cause the light source to emit a more intense, blinding light for 24 hours.
data.level3Description: Infuse Shadowlight into all allies within melee range of you, rolling a D4. If you roll a 1 or a 2, then all affected allies gain a +3 to their 2 lowest stats for an hour. If you roll a 3 or a 4, then all affected allies gain a +3 to their 2 highest stats for an hour.
data.level4Description: You fire a bolt of Shadowlight. Roll a D4. If you roll a 1 or a 2, then you damage the lowest Health enemy within three turns of you for 5+D5 damage. If you roll a 3 or a 4, then you heal the lowest Health ally within three turns of you for 5+D5 health.
data.level5Description: When you use a level of a Shadowlight ability, you can spend 3 Focus to reroll the D4 roll, taking the new result instead. This does not take an action to do, and cannot be used to reroll a dice you have already rerolled. This does not take an action to do.

data.abilityDescription: You are tune with the animals of the world, able to sense their presence, command them and ally with them. Even hostile animals instinctively pull back when attacking you, unwilling to harm you.
data.level1Description: You reach out with your mind, sensing the number and locations of any animals within a mile of you.
data.level2Description: When an animal goes to target you with an attack or an ability, there is a 25% chance that they will instead choose to target someone else, unless you are the only target within attackable range.
data.level3Description: Issue a command to an animal close to you that you can see. The animal will attempt to carry out that command.
data.level4Description: Any attacks made against you by animals you deal half damage.
data.level5Description: You can now get an animal you encounter to aid you as a companion for a day, by passing a Charisma (Animal Handling) check against their Willpower (Pressure). The Focus cost of this ability varies from 5-20 depending on the power of the beast, with more powerful beasts costing more. This ability costs half Focus if you fail the check. You can only have one beast companion at a time.

data.abilityDescription: Before leaving his people, Faribir the Shamed went to the All-Machine that rules his people, asking for a boon to help him on his journey. The All-Machine produced for him a cutting-edge device, capable of rewinding time, although its capabilities are limited.
data.level1Description: Rewind time around a wound that has been inflicted on you in battle, negating D6 damage. This can only be used immediately after the damage has been inflicted and cannot be used to heal more damage than was dealt to you. Using this ability uses up your next major action.
data.level2Description: Rewind time, erasing the last thing you or an ally said.
data.level3Description: You can rewind time after sleeping to get more sleep, removing any tiredness debuffs. This can be used on allies as well as yourself at a cost of 5 Focus per person. Some sleep has to have occurred to use this ability.
data.level4Description: Rewind time, rerolling a dice roll which has just happened. The new roll is taken regardless of whether it is better or worse than the original. This only costs a minor action if used in combat.
data.level5Description: Rewind time on an item, reverting it to a previous state. This can be used to recharge drained items, repair damaged items, or break recently repaired items.

data.abilityDescription: Whilst you lack the facilities to forge your own weapons, you can sharpen, streamline and alter the blades, handles and blunt edges of melee weapons, making them more accurate and potent.
data.level1Description: Enhance the grip of a melee weapon, giving anyone who uses it a +2 to hit with it until the end of combat. This can be done as a minor action.
data.level2Description: Add to the damaging edge of a melee weapon, causing it to deal an extra 2 damage until the end of combat. This can be done as a minor action.
data.level3Description: Tinker with the reach of a melee weapon, allowing it to attack targets one turn away as if they were in melee. This lasts until the end of combat and can be done as a minor action.
data.level4Description: Streamline a melee weapon, meaning that if you kill an enemy with your attack, you may attack again against a different enemy for no action. This can only be done once per player per round. Changing a weapon in this way can be done as a minor action.
data.level5Description: The effects of this ability now last for 24 hours, instead of until the end of the current combat.

data.abilityDescription: As you run at an enemy, you trample them beneath your feet, injuring them even if your initial strike misses.
data.level1Description: If you move into melee with an enemy and attack them in the same turn (such as when you Charge), you deal D6 damage to them. This damage is dealt even if the attack misses.

data.abilityDescription: You are specialised in the study of weaponry. Whilst this does not translate to combat skill, you know about weapons of all kinds, and can use your knowledge of weapons to glean information about places and people.
data.level1Description: You have a unique specialty: Intelligence (Weapons), and gain two specialties in Intelligence (Weapons). You can make an Intelligence (Weapons) check instead of Perception (Evaluation) when evaluating weapons.
data.level2Description: When talking with academics or individuals with a strong interest in learning, you can add your Intelligence modifier to Charisma checks, instead of using your Charisma modifier.
data.level3Description: You can make an Intelligence (Weapons) check instead of an Intelligence (Tactics) check when using the Pick Up Enemy Weapon combat manoeuvre.
data.level4Description: When in an area, you are aware of any weapons unique to the area, or weapons who are made solely in this area. This includes any legendary or mythical weapons.
data.level5Description: If you can see an individual’s weapon, you can make an Intelligence (Weapons) check to learn about the history or culture of their people, instead of having to make an Intelligence (Cultures) check. You can also make an Intelligence (Weapons) check instead of Perception (Empathy) to learn about the general temperament of the person.

data.abilityDescription: You fire a barrage of quick, low-damage shots, tearing through lightly armoured foes and inflicting bloody wounds.
data.level1Description: You launch a barrage of (D3+1) shots at an enemy. Each shot does 2 damage to the enemy.
data.level2Description: You launch a barrage of (D5+1) shots at an enemy. Each shot does 2 damage to the enemy.
data.level3Description: You launch a barrage of (D5+1) shots at an enemy. Each shot does 2 damage to the enemy, and causes them to take 1 damage, ignoring armour,  on their next turn.
data.level4Description: You launch a barrage of (D3+3) shots at an enemy. Each shot does 2 damage to the enemy, and causes them to take 1 damage, ignoring armour, on their next turn.
data.level5Description: You launch a barrage of (D3+3) shots at an enemy. Each shot does 2 damage to the enemy, and causes them to take 1 damage, ignoring armour, on their next turn. Each shot can target a different enemy.

data.abilityDescription: At your belt is a small collection of vials, each one containing samples of different poisons. These poisons can weaken, burn and confuse your opponents, causing a variety of horrible effects.
data.level1Description: You poison a target in melee range with a debilitating toxin, causing them to suffer a -3 to two stats of your choice. After one round of being poisoned, the target can attempt to shake off the poison with a 17+ Endurance (Toxicity) check. The enemy may attempt this check once a round until they succeed, although the check takes a minor action to do. The check difficulty lowers by 3 for every failed check to shake off the poison.
data.level2Description: You poison a target in melee range with hallucinogenic spores, causing them to suffer terrifying hallucinations. Every round, the target must make a 13+ Willpower (Courage) check, losing their major action if they fail, and their minor action if they succeed. After one round of being poisoned, the target can attempt to shake off the poison with a 17+ Willpower (Resistance) check. The enemy may attempt this check once a round until they succeed, and this check does not take an action to do. The check difficulty lowers by 3 for every failed check to shake off the poison.
data.level3Description: You can now stealthily poison a target without them realizing when in Stealth.
data.level4Description: You poison a target in melee range with an acidic venom, causing them to take 4D4 damage on their turn. After one round of being poisoned, the target can attempt to shake off the poison with a 17+ Endurance (Pain) check. The enemy may attempt this check once a round until they succeed, although the check takes a minor action to do. The check difficulty lowers by 3 for every failed check to shake off the poison.
data.level5Description: You poison a target in melee range with a custom concoction, causing them to suffer the effects of your debilitating toxin, hallucinogenic spores and acidic venom simultaneously. After one round of being poisoned, the target can attempt to shake off the poison with a 26+ Endurance (Toxicity) check. The enemy may attempt this check once a round until they succeed, and this does not take an action to do. The check difficulty lowers by 4 for every failed check to shake off the poison.

data.abilityDescription: You connect two people up to your equaliser, a complex device which heals and equalises mass and matter, spreading injuries between the two.
data.level1Description: Pick two allies within one turn of you, or yourself and one ally within one turn of you. The two individuals Health is combined, then split evenly between the two individuals. This cannot raise an individuals Health above it’s Max Health.

What form your robot takes should be  discussed with your GM before the start of the adventure, You construct your robot’s stats using points (more information is in the Supporting Documentation for this ability). data.abilityDescription: You are a patient fighter. Expertly dodging your opponent’s attacks, you wait for the perfect moment, before unleashing a devastating strike capable of felling enemies in a single strike.
data.level1Description: Each round, you gain a +2 to dodge if you could've launched an attack that round but choose not to, excluding counterattacks. This stacks for every consecutive turn you do not launch an attack, up to a +10 to dodge.
data.level2Description: When you are rolling to dodge, if you successfully dodge with a final check results that is at least 12 above the enemy’s attacking check, you can launch a counterattack against that enemy. If you counterattack and your final check result is above a 20, your counterattack deals maximum weapon damage.
data.level3Description: You can activate this as an enemy attacks you. You gain a +5 to dodge, but the enemy gets to make two attacks against you. This does not take an action to do.
data.level4Description: When you launch a counterattack, you can spend 5 Focus to have your counterattack automatically hit. This must be done before rolling to hit and does not take an action to do.
data.level5Description: When you deal damage with your weapon, if you deal half or less of your weapon’s maximum damage, you can cancel the attack and give yourself a bonus to Dexterity (Dodging) equal to the damage you would have dealt. This bonus disappears after your next Dexterity (Dodging) check.

data.abilityDescription: You can see souls within anything with a soul, and around anything that uses souls, be it magic or technology.
data.level1Description: You can see souls for one minute. Souls appear as glowing, multicoloured balls within anything with a soul, and anything that uses souls in any way. You cannot move whilst your Soul Vision is active.
data.level2Description: You can now move whilst your Soul Vision is active.
data.level3Description: Your Soul Vision now lasts for ten minutes.
data.level4Description: When activating your Soul Vision, you can spend an extra 2 Focus to see souls even through a surface, although you cannot see them if they are behind multiple surfaces.
data.level5Description: Your Soul Vision is now always active as a permanent passive effect. Level 4 of this ability is now activated independently to allow you to see souls through a single surface for ten minutes.

data.abilityDescription: You have spent lots of time in space and are an expert in most experts of space travel, with extensive knowledge of space and its contents, and a knack for identifying your position when in space.
data.level1Description: You have a +3 to any checks involving space, travelling through space, or knowledge of things that may be found/occur in space. You instantly know where you are in space at all times, and know of any nearby planets/space features such as asteroids, nebulas etc.

data.level1Description:
You have a D4 weapon (the type of weapon is up to you and your GM). You can attack with this weapon as a minor action but can only attack with this weapon once on your turn. 
Once you hit Level 3, this damage of this weapon upgrades to a D6, and when you hit Level 7, it upgrades to a D8.

data.level1Description:
Disrupt a vehicle system and make an Intelligence (Computing) check. That system is counted as destroyed for a period of time relating to your check result:
6 (or below): 1 round
7-14: 2 rounds
15+: 3 rounds
During this time, the system cannot be repaired. After the time has passed, the system returns to its previous functionality.

data.abilityDescription:
You spray gouts of flame at your enemies, engulfing them and their allies and burning them to the bone, although you can sometimes burn yourself in your zeal.

Requires Generate Heat ability
data.level1Description: You have a 3+D3 Flame Spray (Ranged Only) weapon. Attacking with your Flame Spray generates 1 Heat.
data.level2Description: Your Flame Spray can be used in melee range. Using your Flame Spray in melee range causes you to take damage equal to half the damage dealt to your target. Attacking with your Flame Spray in melee range generates 3 Heat.
data.level3Description: Your Flame Spray now deals 4+D6 damage.
data.level4Description: When you attack with your Flame Spray, you can choose to deal half damage to all targets in melee range of your original target. This must be done before rolling for damage. Attacking in this way generates 2 Heat instead of 1.
data.level5Description: You take half damage from all fire damage.

data.abilityDescription: Whilst you still require specific ingredients to make professional Healing and Focus potions, you can mix together various herbs to create weaker salves with different effects, as well as rare potions using strange ingredients.
data.level1Description: You can gather Herbs around the world. When out of combat, you can use 3 Herbs to restore 1 Health, or 2 Herbs to restore 1 Focus.
data.level2Description: Create a Healing Salve that heals for ½ X Health. A Healing Salve must be made out of combat, and can be stored for later use once made.
data.level3Description: Create a Focus Unguent that restores X Focus. A Focus Unguent must be made out of combat and can be stored for later use once made.
data.level4Description: Create a Leatherskin Potion that gives whoever drinks it 2 Natural Armour for 24 hours. This potion can only be made out of combat and can be stored for later use.
data.level5Description:
Once a day, you can make an INT (Nature) roll. If you roll an 11 or below, nothing happens. If you roll 11-16, you learn the rough location and effect of a random rare plant. If you roll a 17+, you can specify a location, or effect, of a plant you would like to learn about. 
You can use these rare plants to make slaves and potions with varying effects. These creations will also have a focus and herb cost to create, as determined by the GM, and can only be made out of combat.

data.abilityDescription: You are always on the lookout for interesting or sensational information, although you are less concerned with the accuracy of the information and are even willing to create and spread gossip yourself.
data.level1Description: You have a +3 to Charisma checks when trying to get someone to tell you speculative information or gossip about a person or place.
data.level2Description: You are aware of rumours, myths and legends regarding your current location.
data.level3Description: When interacting with a group or organisation, remember two pieces of information about that group. One of these pieces of information is true, or based in truth, whilst the other is completely false. You are unaware of which piece of information is true.
data.level4Description: When in a public area, you can spend two hours to learn a piece of information relating to a topic of your choice. The GM determines how accurate this information is by rolling a D20, with a higher result being more accurate information. You do not get to know the dice result.
data.level5Description: Make a Charisma (Deception) check to spread a rumour of your choice amongst the people you are with over the course of six hours. How far the rumour spreads and how many people believe it depends on how much Focus you spend, how high your Deception check result is and how believable the rumour is.

data.abilityDescription: Chasing down a fleeing opponent, you lash out with your weapon, halting and potentially damaging them.
data.level1Description: When you succeed in chasing a fleeing target, you launch an attack against them.

data.abilityDescription: You fight with honour and dignity, refusing to deal underhanded blows and even returning a disarmed enemy’s weapon to them. This strengthens your resolve, pushing you to greater feats of heroism and battle prowess.
data.level1Description: Launch an attack against an enemy. This attack automatically hits and deals maximum weapon damage. After the attack, the enemy gets to attack you, assuming they survive. This attack automatically hits and deals maximum weapon damage.
data.level2Description: When you are going to counter an enemy or deal a critical hit, you can instead not counter/treat the attack as a normal attack. If you do this, you gain +4 to hit against that enemy for the rest of the fight. This ability can stack multiple times during a battle.
data.level3Description: If you are going to deal X damage to an enemy, you can negate that damage for 4 Focus. The enemy’s next successful attack deals X less damage to you. This ability can be done as a minor action.
data.level4Description: If you are fighting against a number of enemies equal to the number of combatants on your side (including yourself), then all attacks deal half damage to you.
data.level5Description: When you disarm an enemy, you can choose not to disarm them. That enemy deals 2 less damage to you for the rest of the fight. This can only stack to a maximum of minus 4 damage a fight from Levels 1-9, and minus 6 damage a fight from Level 10+.

data.abilityDescription: As an enemy strikes out at you, you strike their arm, taking their weapon and lashing out at them with it, potentially leaving the weapon stuck in them.
data.level1Description: When an enemy attacks you with a melee weapon and misses, spend 7 Focus to take their weapon and attack them with it. You are considered skilled with that weapon for the purposes of this attack. After the attack, the weapon stays stuck in the enemy (if you hit) or is dropped to the ground (if you missed). The enemy can retrieve their weapon either way using a minor action. This ability does not take an action to do.

This cannot be used to control Old Human technology.

data.abilityDescription: You warp spacetime, opening glowing portals that can be used to transport items, or even people between them, allowing for quick getaways or the bypassing of defences.
data.level1Description: Create two small circular portals, each half a metre in diameter, by touching two areas. You can pass a small, non-organic item through the portals. The portals close after something passes through them, or after one hour. You can also close the portals early.
data.level2Description: You can now pass organic material through the portals.
data.level3Description: You can now create a portal at any location within 10 metres you can see, rather than needing to touch an area.
data.level4Description: Create two circular human-sized portals at any location you can see within 10 metres. The portal closes after something passes through it, or after one hour. You can also close the portals early. You cannot pass a conscious, unwilling living thing through the portal.
data.level5Description: After something passes through one of your portals, you can spend 3 Focus to keep the portal open. This can be used multiple times on the same portal.

data.abilityDescription: In combat, you carefully line up long-distance shots, honing in on your target until you finally fire with pinpoint accuracy, potentially killing foes in a single shot.
data.level1Description: If you are wielding a two-handed ranged weapon, you can attack enemies that are two turns away without suffering a penalty to hit. The other levels of this ability can also only be used when wielding a two-handed ranged weapon.
data.level2Description: If you do not move or change location on your turn, you gain a +2 to hit. This stacks up to a maximum of +6 to hit after not changing location for three rounds, and resets when you move or change location.
data.level3Description: Line up a shot on an enemy, adding a D6 to your next weapon attack against them. This cannot be used to add more than 3D6 to your damage against an enemy. This can only be used on one enemy at a time.
data.level4Description: If you do not attack an enemy on your turn, gain 3 Focus.
data.level5Description: Levels 1 and 2 of this ability now stack indefinitely, with no upper limit to hit/limit on your bonus to hit or how many D6s can be added to your damage.

data.abilityDescription: You release a burst of healing energy or chemicals into the air, filling the air and causing the wounds of all those nearby to start knitting together.
data.level1Description: Heal yourself and all nearby allies for 3 Health.

data.abilityDescription: You are able to manipulate Luck, gaining the ability to manipulate luck depending on how much bad luck you have experienced. This allows you to bless you and your allies with good luck and curse your enemies with bad luck.
data.level1Description:
You store Luck, up to a maximum of 100. Every time you roll a 4 or below on a D20, you gain the amount below 5 in Luck. You gain an extra 3 Luck every time you or an ally rolls a natural 1.

You can spend 2 Luck to increase the result of a check you make by 1. This can be used multiple times on a single check and cannot be used to increase the result beyond what you could achieve by rolling a 20. This does not take an action to do in combat.
data.level2Description:
You now gain Luck every time you roll a 9 or below on a D20 and gain the amount below 10 in Luck.

You can now spend 2 Luck to increase the result of a check an ally makes by 1. This can be used multiple times on a single check and cannot be used to increase the result beyond what they could achieve by rolling a 20. This does not take an action to do in combat.
data.level3Description: You now gain 4 Luck whenever you roll minimum damage on a damage roll, or when you fail a check you have a specialty in.
data.level4Description: You can now spend 2 Luck to reduce the result of a check by 1. You can also now use Luck to affect the result of any check made by someone in your presence, whether they are an ally or an enemy. This can be used multiple times on a single check and cannot be used to decrease the result below what they could achieve by rolling a 1. This does not take an action to do in combat.
data.level5Description: If you increase a check result to what it would be if the target rolled a 20, it counts as a natural 20. If you decrease a check result to what it would be if the target rolled a 1, it counts as a natural 1.

data.abilityDescription: You send shadows into the eyes of enemies, clouding their vision and making it impossible for them to see.
data.level1Description: Send shadows into the eyes of enemies, blinding them for two rounds. Whilst blinded, enemies fail all Perception (Seeing) checks and suffer a -5 to Strength (Attacking) checks.

data.level2Description: When you need to make a Charisma (Etiquette) check, you can instead make a Charisma (Deception) check.
data.level3Description: Whenever you lose when gambling, or during other games of chance, you talk the winner into giving back 10% of any money you gambled.
